title: mcp: a skill that serves only the in-product agents is still projected as an MCP prompt when its bound tools happen to be served, and a host has no way to say so
body:
repo:cloud#3 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbZqfEd7pcckjz3pGqn

Filing category: ① product defect (residual of #32767). Filed by the cloud lane; first touch (domain, queue) is left to triage. Drafted by the cloud#4337 card thread from a static reading at pin `b914e7247f`.
reach: public entry `/api/v1/mcp` (`prompts/list`, `prompts/get`) on any connection whose token carries `data:write` or `actions:execute`.
Related: objectstack-ai/cloud#4337 (blocked on this card), objectstack#32767 (closed by PR #32880 `b4f69716e7`), objectstack#32885.

## Business reason

An MCP agent (Claude Code, Cursor) follows the prompts the server lists. Cloud registers the playbooks of its in-product `ask` / `build` agents as `skill` metadata, because those agents resolve their skills from it. Those playbooks are written for the in-product tool set and the in-product approval card. When one reaches an MCP client, the agent calls tools that connection never lists and promises the user a confirmation card that never appears. Cloud filters these rows today through a proxy over the `mcp` service (cloud PR #4419, `packages/service-ai-studio/src/mcp-skill-prompts.ts`). Cloud wants to drop that proxy, and it can't while two of its rows still pass the framework's test.

## What happens at b914e7247f

#32880 offers a skill only when the connection serves every tool in its `tools` binding (`packages/mcp/src/skill-prompts.ts:188`, `skillBindingServed` at `:232`, `bindingEntryServed` at `:210`). That withholds 8 of cloud's 10 rows on every connection, because each binds a tool only the in-product agents have. Two rows bind only tools that MCP also serves, so they pass:

1. **`record_writing`** binds `create_record` and `update_record` (cloud `packages/service-ai-studio/src/skills/record-writing-skill.ts:30`). The MCP data door serves both names (`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts:2955`, `:2982`) on a `data:write` connection. Its instructions (`record-writing-skill.ts:29`) tell the agent to call `open_record`, which no MCP connection lists, and say "the user confirms on a card", which is the in-product approval card. MCP has no such card.
2. **`actions_executor`** binds `action_*` (cloud `packages/service-ai-studio/src/skills/actions-executor-skill.ts:47`). `TOOL_FAMILY_DOORS` (`skill-prompts.ts:207`) counts an `action_` binding as served wherever `run_action` is (`mcp-http-tools.ts:3294`, gated on `actions:execute` at `:3253`). Its instructions (`actions-executor-skill.ts:43`) tell the agent to call `action_<object>__<action>` tools, which MCP never lists (MCP reaches actions only through `list_actions` / `run_action`), and to fall back on the in-product confirm card.

The binding is the right test for "can this connection run the playbook". It can't answer "is this playbook written for MCP at all": a skill can bind tools MCP serves under the same names and still be written for a different agent loop. #32767's Expected asked for the binding test "and/or a declared host seam to withhold skills per request". PR #32880 delivered the first half only.

## What cloud needs

A skill that serves only the in-product agents is never projected as an MCP prompt, on any connection, whatever its binding. The owner of the skill declares this. Cloud does not need it to be per-request. The shape is the framework's call (for example a declared property on the skill, or a host seam on the skill bridge). This card names the need, not a key.

## Done when

- A skill declared in-product-only is absent from `prompts/list` and unknown to `prompts/get` on every MCP connection, including one that serves every tool it binds. A pin test uses a skill that binds `create_record` / `update_record` on a `data:write` connection.
- A skill without the declaration is projected exactly as at b914e7247f. The #32767 binding test is unchanged.
- The declaration does not change how the in-product agents resolve or offer the skill.
- Docs for the `skill` type (and #32885's text on `SkillSchema.tools`) say how a skill opts out of MCP projection.
- Cloud then marks its in-product rows, drops `mcp-skill-prompts.ts`, and adds `data:write` and `actions:execute` tokens to `apps/objectos/test/mcp-served-guidance-4337.e2e.test.ts` (that test mints only `data:read` and `metadata:write` today, at `:205`–`:206`). That is cloud#4337's remaining half, not this card.

## Dedupe

Words searched: `skill prompt MCP projection` (72 hits; only #32767 is about this, closed), `skillBindingServed` (2 hits: #32767, #32885, both closed and both about the binding test). Suggested dedupe words: skill MCP projection opt-out, in-product skill prompts/list, skill not projected MCP, host withhold skill prompt, record_writing prompt MCP.
